 MCMC appoints service provider for RM2.7bil undersea cable project
 MCMC appoints service provider for RM2.7bil undersea cable project
 17-Nov-2026, 16:27 17 Nov 2026, 16:27 Bernama Share This will provide more reliable digital services to the community, businesses and government.
 The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission said the Madani submarine cable project would boost the capacity and resilience of the country’s communications network. 
 CYBERJAYA : The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) has appointed TM Technology Services Sdn Bhd (TM) as the universal service provider for designing, implementing, and operating the Madani Submarine Cable Connection System (Salam) worth RM2.7 billion. 
 MCMC said in a statement that the project would be funded through the Universal Service Provision (USP) Fund.
 The Salam system will enhance communication connection capacity between Peninsular Malaysia, Sabah and Sarawak.
 “It simultaneously supports the provision of more reliable digital services to the community, businesses and government. In addition, it will also provide an alternative route for data traffic, thereby reducing the risk of service disruption in the event the existing undersea cables experience interference or damage,” said MCMC.
 With a length of approximately 5,500km, the system will be implemented by TM based on Alcatel Submarine Networks’s (ASN) submarine cable technology and will meet increasing demand.
 The capacity utilisation of the existing submarine cable network, which has been in operation since 2017, has now reached about 85%.
 MCMC said the Salam system would include 10 new submarine cable landing stations, namely Cherating and Sedili in Peninsular Malaysia; Kuching, Sibu (Matu) and Bintulu (Samalaju) in Sarawak; as well as Kota Kinabalu, Kudat, Pulau Banggi, Sandakan and Tawau in Sabah.
 The additional capacity will support the expansion of broadband and 5G networks, cloud services, artificial intelligence, and data centres, thereby providing a stronger foundation to expand digital capacity, particularly in Sabah and Sarawak.
 “Four pairs of optical fibre will be dedicated to meet the strategic needs of the nation, including sovereign cloud infrastructure, government digital services and cybersecurity.
 “Salam reflects MCMC’s commitment to strengthening Malaysia’s digital infrastructure so that more communities and businesses can enjoy the benefits of the digital economy,” said MCMC.
 The implementation of the Salam project is scheduled to begin in mid-December and it is expected to be completed in phases by the first quarter of 2030.
 Earlier, Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim and French president Emmanuel Macron witnessed the exchange of a memorandum of understanding between TM and ASN at the Sultan Abdul Samad Building in Kuala Lumpur.
